requirements.title: Type-declaration statement envelope
requirements.definition: A declaration-type-spec precedes a nonempty entity-decl list. The intervening group can be omitted, can consist of a double colon alone, or can contain comma-prefixed attribute specifications followed by the double colon. Attributes do not remove their own entity/scope restrictions. C806 independently requires the separator when an entity has initialization.

Intrinsic, TYPE-intrinsic/derived/enum/enumeration, CLASS-derived/unlimited, TYPE-assumed, TYPEOF and CLASSOF retain R703 and its conditions; no unapproved source-use prototype is required.

requirements.oracle: Compile admission and two focused grammar/report-control contrasts; source-use relationships import no execution credit until independently supported. Reporting capability accepts an ordinary successful or unsuccessful compiler return only with the intended located report.

requirements.title: Nineteen attribute-spec alternatives
requirements.definition: The permitted alternatives are access-spec, ALLOCATABLE, ASYNCHRONOUS, CODIMENSION with bracketed coarray-spec, CONTIGUOUS, DIMENSION with parenthesized array-spec, EXTERNAL, INTENT with intent-spec, INTRINSIC, language-binding-spec, OPTIONAL, PARAMETER, POINTER, PROTECTED, rank-clause, SAVE, TARGET, VALUE and VOLATILE. This is a syntax list, not permission to use every attribute on every data object or function, or to combine incompatible attributes. RANK is a DIMENSION-specifying clause, not a separate semantic attribute.

Procedure-pointer dummy intent remains a separate canonical role, not an ordinary procedure receiving data intent.

requirements.oracle: Nineteen pending bounded syntax/context plans with canonical semantic ownership. Admissions are positive controls, not effects. Attribute incompatibilities belong to their defining C rules; no omnibus negative is inferred from the list.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A successful declaration does not prove allocation, asynchronous communication, volatility, SAVE retention or coarray execution. No new profile, companion, compiler probe or source-use link is included.

requirements.title: No repeated attribute specification in one declaration
requirements.definition: Within one type-declaration statement the same attr-spec may occur at most once. This statement-local relation is not the same as explicitly specifying an attribute in separate statements, which remains C815. The finite repeated-specification contrasts use identical keywords and payloads; mixed PUBLIC/PRIVATE, conflicting INTENT values, and RANK/DIMENSION interactions are not silently treated as the same isolated condition.

pending.duplicate-pointer: PENDING scalar INTEGER data pointer with POINTER twice and no initializer. Remove one POINTER; never inquire about undefined association or convert the condition into a target/lifetime error.
pending.duplicate-protected: PENDING module INTEGER variable with PROTECTED twice and no COMMON. Remove one specification only; foreign variable-definition restrictions are not this condition.
pending.duplicate-rank: PENDING ALLOCATABLE INTEGER with identical RANK(1) clauses, no entity array-spec. Remove one RANK clause, preserving C864 eligibility and deferred shape.
pending.duplicate-save: PENDING ordinary local INTEGER variable with two SAVE specifications and no initializer or COMMON. Delete one keyword; do not confuse this with permitted confirmation of an implicit SAVE.

pending.duplicate-volatile: PENDING local INTEGER variable with VOLATILE twice and no INTENT(IN), use/host or coarray complications. Remove one specification only.

requirements.title: A NAME binding specifier limits the declaration list
requirements.definition: When a type declaration's language-binding-spec includes NAME=, exactly one entity-decl is allowed. The condition is presence of the specifier, including an empty or all-blank value, not whether a nonblank external label results. Without NAME=, this particular constraint does not limit the list to one entity; all other BIND/data constraints still apply.

requirements.title: BIND in a type declaration excludes procedure names
requirements.definition: A type-declaration statement containing a language-binding-spec cannot have a procedure name in its entity list. This does not prohibit interoperable procedures declared by their proper FUNCTION/SUBROUTINE/interface syntax. A procedure with BIND requires an explicit interface independently of whether it is called.

requirements.title: Object and function entity-declarator alternatives
requirements.definition: The object alternative consists of an object-name followed, in order, by optional parenthesized array-spec, optional bracketed coarray-spec, optional star char-length and optional initialization. The other alternative is a function-name with only an optional star char-length. Names have their actual semantic roles; a result object declared inside an internal or module function is not automatically a forbidden declaration of that function name.

requirements.title: PARAMETER declarations initialize every entity

requirements.title: Entity categories that cannot have declaration initialization
requirements.definition: An object declarator cannot have initialization when it names a dummy argument, a function result, a named-COMMON object outside BLOCK DATA, any blank-COMMON object, an allocatable variable or an automatic data object. Only the named-COMMON category has the BLOCK DATA exception. These are properties of the declared entity itself, not a recursive ban on a derived object merely because a component is allocatable or default-initialized.

Delete only declaration initialization. The repaired function still defines its result and does not specify the function name illegally under C1570.

A separate source-use contrast records that BLOCK DATA does not provide the named-COMMON exception to blank COMMON; C1415/C1416 must be discharged before a second negative is proposed.

Initialization-implied SAVE/C814 is tightly coupled and must not replace the C808 cause.

Retain 7.5.10/10.1.12 qualifications; the object itself is not ALLOCATABLE. No unallocated component payload is read.

requirements.definition: Arrow initialization requires the declared entity to have POINTER. Equals initialization excludes POINTER. This does not reinterpret equals as association, and it is not scalar value broadcasting into a pointer target.
